writeup.headline: MKS rates Hold: strong growth is offset by heavy debt, a weak share-price trend and full valuation.
writeup.thesis: MKS scores 48, a Hold, just 4 points above the Sell band and 17 short of Buy. Growth is the clear strength (score 84), with latest-quarter revenue growth of 28.3% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 16.3%, and growth sped up by 13.1 pp from the previous quarter. The balance sheet drags hardest (score 7): net debt is 7.67 times free cash flow and cash covers only 0.12 of debt. Valuation scores 36. In absolute terms the stock is not cheap at 32.4x free cash flow and 26.8x EV/EBIT, with an FCF yield 1.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history it is expensive, more expensive than at 50 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S. The trend score of 26 reflects a price 50.9% below its 52-week high and 21.5% below its 200-day average, while quality is middling at a 15.7% operating margin with diluted share count up 7.9% year on year.
key_risks: High leverage: net debt at 7.67 times free cash flow and cash covering only 0.12 of debt.
Weak price trend: shares 26.7 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days and 50.9% below the 52-week high.
Valuation is not low in absolute terms and is expensive against its own history on P/S and P/FCF.
Shareholder dilution, with diluted share count up 7.9% year on year.
Q3 results on Nov 4 and tariff exposure noted in guidance could disappoint; the Ophir sale still needs approvals.
what_would_change: Down: a 4-point drop in the score, for example from weaker growth or a further slide in the trend factor, would move the rating to Sell.
Up: reaching Buy needs 17 more points, most plausibly from debt reduction (e.g. Ophir sale proceeds of $650M) lifting the balance-sheet score from 7.
Up: a recovery in the share price toward its 50- and 200-day averages would raise the trend score from 26.
Either way: Q3 results on Nov 4 confirming or reversing the growth acceleration would shift the growth score of 84.
